log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Sneasler

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott and Gholdengo to threaten immediate Tailwind plus spread Steel damage while pressuring Sneasler and Fairy targets. Mega Tyranitar provides a durable offensive answer to Gardevoir, Skarmory, and Sinistcha; Milotic punishes Incineroar’s Intimidate and checks Fire-types. Lopunny is less reliable into Protect, Intimidate, and Sneasler.
decisions.notebook: Preferred game-plan is Whimsicott/Gholdengo lead with Tailwind support and Make It Rain pressure. Milotic is the primary Incineroar counter and benefits from Competitive when Intimidated. Mega Tyranitar is reserved for strong physical pressure into Gardevoir, Skarmory, and Sinistcha, while Lopunny is a flexible Fake Out/Fighting option when immediate tempo is more valuable.

decisions.rationale: Lead Incineroar+Sneasler: Intimidate+Fake Out+Wisp neuters the physical core (Tyranitar/Arcanine/Lopunny), while Sneasler's Close Combat OHKOs Mega Tyranitar and Lopunny through their sets. Gardevoir-Mega backs with Pixilate Hyper Voice and Shadow Ball for Gholdengo; Sinistcha's Rage Powder redirects and Matcha Gotcha pressures Milotic. This 4 covers every opposing threat and keeps speed control flexible.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leans physical (Mega Tyranitar, Arcanine, Lopunny) plus special Gholdengo/Milotic/Whimsicott. Whimsicott is Prankster Tailwind+Encore+Helping Hand, Focus Sash, Timid. Gholdengo Good-as-Gold (immune to status), Life Orb, Modest, Nasty Plot+Make It Rain+Shadow Ball. Milotic Competitive (Intimidate triggers it) with Scald/Ice Beam/Haze, Sitrus. Arcanine Intimidate+Shuca, Careful. Lopunny Limber, BlackBelt, Fake Out/HJK/Triple Axel, fast. Tyranitar Mega Sand Stream, Adamant. Plan: Incineroar Intimidate/Wisp/Fake Out/Parting Shot vs physical; Sneasler Focus Sash+Unburden Close Combat kills Tyranitar/Lopunny, Shadow Claw for Gholdengo; Gardevoir-Mega Pixilate Hyper Voice + Shadow Ball; Sinistcha Rage Powder redirect + Strength Sap + Matcha Gotcha for Milotic. Watch Milotic's Competitive when Incineroar Intimidates. Gholdengo immune to Wisp/status. Whimsicott outspeeds most; consider Tailwind counter or priority.

decisions.rationale: Set Tailwind immediately so Gholdengo moves ahead of Sneasler from the next turn, while spread Make It Rain applies pressure to both foes. Fake Out cannot affect Gholdengo, and this preserves Whimsicott’s support role and Focus Sash protection.
decisions.notebook: Preferred game plan remains Whimsicott/Gholdengo Tailwind plus Make It Rain pressure. Milotic is the primary Incineroar counter and can exploit Competitive; Mega Tyranitar is reserved for physical pressure into Gardevoir, Skarmory, and Sinistcha. Lopunny is the flexible Fake Out/Fighting option when immediate tempo is more valuable.

decisions.rationale: Switch Milotic in as the safest Incineroar answer while preserving Mega Tyranitar for the opposing backline. Gholdengo passes because it cannot safely attack into the current board and should avoid further unnecessary exposure.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Incineroar has Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot, Will-O-Wisp, and Sitrus Berry. Sneasler has Focus Sash, Unburden, and revealed Dire Claw. Preserve Milotic as the primary Incineroar counter and Mega Tyranitar for pressure into Gardevoir, Skarmory, and Sinistcha. Consider a less vulnerable anti-lead plan in later games.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out flinches Whimsicott (priority +3 beats Prankster Tailwind) to deny speed control; Sneasler's 4x Dire Claw is a guaranteed OHKO that pops Whimsicott's Focus Sash, leaving it at 1 HP and flinched for an easy clean-up. Gholdengo's Make It Rain is resisted by Incineroar and Sneasler holds Focus Sash, so the opening is safe.

Watch Milotic's Competitive when Incineroar Intimidates. Gholdengo immune to Wisp/status. Whimsicott outspeeds most; deny Tailwind with priority.

decisions.rationale: Protect Gholdengo from Sneasler’s faster super-effective Shadow Claw while Milotic pressures the 14% Sneasler with Scald. This preserves the key Incineroar counter and lets Gholdengo safely threaten Sneasler next turn if it protects.
decisions.notebook: Incineroar has Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot, Will-O-Wisp, Flare Blitz, and Sitrus Berry. Sneasler has Focus Sash, Unburden, Jolly nature, and revealed Dire Claw; it is substantially faster than Gholdengo. Preserve Milotic as the primary Incineroar answer and Mega Tyranitar as pressure into Gardevoir, Skarmory, and Sinistcha. Use less vulnerable anti-lead structures in later games, respecting Fake Out plus fast Sneasler pressure.

decisions.rationale: Gholdengo is the main Life Orb threat at 90%. Incineroar Flare Blitz (59.8-130.9%) plus Sneasler Shadow Claw (30.9-69.1%) combined min ~90.7% reliably KOs it even on low rolls. Sneasler at 15% is expendable and dies to Milotic Scald anyway. Avoid Parting Shot: it triggers Milotic's Competitive or fails on Good-as-Gold Gholdengo.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Encore/Helping Hand, Focus Sash, Timid (fainted). Gholdengo Good-as-Gold (status-immune), Life Orb, Modest, Nasty Plot/Make It Rain/Shadow Ball; Make It Rain self-drops SpA. Milotic Competitive (Intimidate/stat-drop triggers +2 SpA), Scald/Ice Beam/Haze, Sitrus, bulky. Arcanine Intimidate+Shuca Careful; Lopunny Limber BlackBelt Fake Out/HJK/Triple Axel fast; Tyranitar Mega Sand Stream Adamant. Plan: KO Gholdengo with Flare Blitz+Shadow Claw; never lower Milotic's stats (no Parting Shot/Intimidate into it). Gardevoir-Mega Pixilate Hyper Voice + Shadow Ball; Sinistcha Rage Powder redirect + Strength Sap + Matcha Gotcha for Milotic. Watch Milotic Competitive when Incineroar Intimidates.

decisions.rationale: Bring Sinistcha: it resists Milotic's Scald (0.5x) and is neutral to Gholdengo's Make It Rain, only fearing Shadow Ball, while Gardevoir is hit super-effectively by both Gholdengo moves. Rage Powder protects Incineroar from Milotic, and Shadow Ball/Matcha Gotcha threaten Gholdengo and Milotic. Incineroar stays in (no switch to avoid re-triggering Intimidate into Milotic's Competitive).

decisions.rationale: Scald pressures the primary Incineroar answer for substantial super-effective damage while preserving Milotic’s role. Gholdengo’s Shadow Ball targets Sinistcha’s 2x weakness and is the strongest way to prevent its sustained support, despite its Speed uncertainty and reduced Special Attack.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Double into Gholdengo to secure the KO: Flare Blitz (59.8-130.9%) + Shadow Ball (43.3-96.3%) combined min ~103% of max, well above its 90% HP. Even if it Protects (success reduced), we lose little: Milotic Scald into Incineroar is only ~30-36% (Sitrus cushions), and Gholdengo's -2 SpA Make It Rain into Sinistcha is only ~19-34%. Removing the Life Orb threat is the priority; Milotic alone is manageable next turn.

Gholdengo Good-as-Gold (status-immune), Life Orb, Modest, Nasty Plot/Make It Rain/Shadow Ball; Make It Rain self-drops SpA; Protect success reduced (used T2). Milotic Competitive (Intimidate/stat-drop triggers +2 SpA), Scald/Ice Beam/Haze, Sitrus, bulky; Scald into Incineroar ~30-36% (not a KO). Arcanine Intimidate+Shuca Careful; Lopunny Limber BlackBelt Fake Out/HJK/Triple Axel fast; Tyranitar Mega Sand Stream Adamant. decisions.rationale: Scald heavily pressures the weakened Incineroar and may KO, while Mega Rock Slide applies spread pressure to both foes, improves Tyranitar’s Speed, and can finish Incineroar or flinch either target. This maximizes immediate board control without wasting Haze or Protect.
decisions.notebook: Milotic remains the primary Incineroar answer. Mega Tyranitar is the preferred evolution and should pressure Gardevoir, Skarmory, and Sinistcha. Incineroar has Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot, Will-O-Wisp, Flare Blitz, and its Sitrus Berry is consumed. Sneasler has Focus Sash, Unburden, Jolly nature, and Dire Claw; it is substantially faster than Gholdengo. In later games, use less vulnerable anti-lead structures and respect Fake Out plus fast Sneasler pressure.

decisions.rationale: Parting Shot into Tyranitar weakens it and safely brings Gardevoir-Mega in after the turn (Rock/Ice are neutral on it, so it's a safe entry). Matcha Gotcha chips both foes super-effectively. Avoids lowering Milotic's stats (Competitive). Even if Incineroar or Sinistcha fall, Gardevoir-Mega remains our win condition.
decisions.notebook: Milotic: Competitive (any stat drop = +2 SpA) — never Intimidate/Parting Shot/Strength Sap it; bulky, Sitrus, Scald/Ice Beam/Haze. Tyranitar: Mega Sand Stream Adamant, physical (Rock Slide/Crunch/Low Kick), can Protect. Gardevoir-Mega: Rock and Ice are NEUTRAL on it (Psychic/Fairy), so it is safe to bring in vs Tyranitar+Milotic; Pixilate Hyper Voice is our spread win condition. Sinistcha Matcha Gotcha is 2x on both foes (~27-59% Tyranitar, ~25-53% Milotic, spread). Milotic outspeeds Sinistcha and its Ice Beam KOs a 40% Sinistcha; Tyranitar vs Sinistcha speed is uncertain. Plan: bring Gardevoir-Mega via Parting Shot (safe post-turn entry), weaken Tyranitar, and grind Milotic with Hyper Voice + Matcha Gotcha; keep Milotic's stats untouched. If Incineroar re-enters later, its Intimidate would trigger Milotic Competitive — avoid that.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Ice Beam guarantees the KO on Sinistcha while Tyranitar uses Crunch to pressure Gardevoir. This avoids Rock Slide’s accuracy risk and prevents Sinistcha from recovering or using Matcha Gotcha; Gardevoir’s Moonblast cannot KO full-health Tyranitar this turn.

Mega Gardevoir Moonblast Tyranitar (2x, ~65-137%, possible OHKO) + Sinistcha Matcha Gotcha (2x both) to remove Tyranitar and chip Milotic. Sinistcha at 15% is expendable and likely dies to Milotic Ice Beam anyway, so use it offensively. Milotic's stats stay untouched (no Competitive trigger).
decisions.notebook: Milotic: Competitive (any stat drop = +2 SpA) — never Intimidate/Parting Shot/Strength Sap it; bulky, Sitrus, Scald/Ice Beam/Haze; Ice Beam can OHKO low Sinistcha. Tyranitar-Mega: Adamant physical (Rock Slide/Crunch/Low Kick), can Protect; Rock Slide ~29-69% on Gardevoir-Mega. Gardevoir-Mega: Pixilate Hyper Voice is the spread win condition (Fairy 2x on Tyranitar ~56-117%, neutral on Milotic ~28-58%); Moonblast 2x on Tyranitar ~65-137%; Rock/Ice neutral on it; Modest, SpA 238, Spe 152 after mega. Sinistcha Matcha Gotcha 2x on both (~25-53% each, spread). Opponent remaining: Milotic + Tyranitar-Mega only (Arcanine/Lopunny not brought). Plan: keep Milotic's stats untouched, remove Tyranitar first, then grind Milotic with Pixilate Hyper Voice. If Incineroar re-enters, its Intimidate would trigger Milotic Competitive — avoid.

reflections.summary: Won because Milotic consistently pressured and removed the Incineroar/Sneasler threats, while Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide flinch and Crunch finished the endgame. Mega Tyranitar was the right Stone holder, but the Whimsicott/Gholdengo lead was more vulnerable to Fake Out plus fast Sneasler pressure than this matchup warranted.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Mega Tyranitar as the evolution, but lead Milotic beside it next game and reserve Whimsicott/Gholdengo. This applies immediate pressure to the opponent’s physical lead structure instead of allowing both fragile leads to be targeted first.
reflections.notebook: Milotic remains the primary Incineroar answer. Mega Tyranitar is the preferred evolution against this composition and pressures Gardevoir and Sinistcha, but Mega Gardevoir’s Moonblast is a major direct threat. The opponent’s preferred pressure pattern combines Fake Out/Intimidate support with fast Sneasler offense; avoid exposing both fragile leads to that combination. Sinistcha has Heatproof and can provide recovery/redirection utility, so apply immediate concentrated damage rather than relying on passive positioning.

reflections.summary: Lost because the team-preview plan gave Milotic a free Competitive boost from Incineroar's Intimidate, and the Sneasler/Incineroar lead was broken by Gholdengo's Protect and Milotic's Scald. Tyranitar-Mega then used Rock Slide spread to KO Incineroar and flinch Sinistcha, and Gardevoir-Mega arrived too late: Moonblast left Tyranitar at 39%, and Crunch KO'd Gardevoir. With zero decision errors, the loss was structural: the brought four and the Gardevoir Mega plan did not neutralize the Milotic/Tyranitar core.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, do not lead Incineroar into Milotic; if Incineroar is brought, keep it off the field until Milotic is gone. Lead Gardevoir-Mega with Sinistcha and double-target Tyranitar immediately with Moonblast + Matcha Gotcha before it can Mega Rock Slide. Gardevoirite is still the right Mega, but Gardevoir must be on the field earlier. Consider replacing Incineroar/Sneasler with a non-Intimidate option if one is available.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Gholdengo leads with Protect when threatened and carries Life Orb; Milotic leads with Scald and will target Sneasler; Tyranitar-Mega uses Rock Slide spread to pressure both slots and Crunch on Gardevoir; Milotic carries Ice Beam for Sinistcha. Strategic facts: Milotic's Competitive makes Intimidate/Parting Shot/Strength Sap on it a losing play; Tyranitar-Mega survives one Gardevoir-Mega Moonblast from full and can KO Gardevoir with Crunch after chip; Rock Slide spread can KO Incineroar and flinch Sinistcha. Future plan: bring Gardevoir-Mega as the Tyranitar answer, but lead it with Sinistcha and remove Tyranitar before it Mega evolves; avoid Incineroar until Milotic is KO'd; if Sneasler is brought, do not waste it on a Protect; expect opponent may bring Arcanine/Lopunny next game.
